## Poison Regression (35p)

```{r}
data("f_data_sm")
#Selecting ligue and creating flag
df<-f_data_sm%>%
  filter(LEAGUE=="Serie A")%>%
  mutate(HA_WIN=ifelse(FTHG>FTAG, 1, ifelse(FTHG==FTAG,0,-1)))

#preprocessing

h<-df%>%mutate(Home=1, ID=1:n())%>%
  select(c("SEASON","HOMETEAM", "AWAYTEAM", "FTHG", "HA_WIN","Home",'ID'))
colnames(h)<-c("Season", "Team", "Opponent", "Goal", "HA_Win", "Home",'ID')


a<-df%>%mutate(Home=0,ID=1:n())%>%
  select(c("SEASON", "AWAYTEAM", "HOMETEAM", "FTAG", "HA_WIN","Home",'ID'))
colnames(a)<-c("Season", "Team", "Opponent", "Goal", "HA_Win", "Home",'ID')




#appending togather


df_f<- rbind(h, a)
```

For this assignment you are going to use the data from the league assigned to you to build Poisson regression model.

### Model Building (10p)

Use all the data except of the last season to build the model (with Home team coefficient).

```{r}
train <- df_f %>% filter(Season!=max(Season))
model <- glm(Goal~Team+Opponent+Home, data=train, family=poisson(link=log))


```

### Prediction (5p)



Make predictions using Skellam distribution for the last season in the dataset.

```{r}
#bellow also we should check availability of teams in test and train sets...

#creating tesiting set
test <- df_f %>%filter(Season==max(Season))
#finding lambda
pred<-predict(model,newdata=test,type="response")
test$lambda<-pred
# now we need to spread date: long to wide, by home column in order to have lambda home/away



test1<-test%>%
  filter(Home==1)%>%
  select(-c(Home,Season,HA_Win))%>%
  rename(Home=Team, Away=Opponent, lambda.H=lambda, Goal.H=Goal)


test2<-test%>%
  filter(Home==0)%>%
  select(-c(Home,Season, HA_Win))%>%
  rename(Home=Opponent, Away=Team, lambda.A=lambda, Goal.A=Goal)


pred_final<-merge(test1,test2, by = 'ID')

#predictions, appllying rowwise

```


```{r}


sk<-function(data,l1,l2,sim=200,action='>'){
  d<-rskellam(sim,mu1 = l1, mu2 = l2)
  
  if (action=='>'){
    return(sum(d>0)/sim)
  }
  else if (action=='0'){
    return(sum(d==0)/sim)
  }else if(action=='<') {
    return(sum(d<0)/sim)
  }
  
  

}





```


### Model Performance (7p)

Define the metric to calculate the efficiency of the predictions.()

```{r}

final<-pred_final%>%
  rowwise()%>%
  mutate(win=sk(l1=lambda.H,l2=lambda.A,action = ">"),
         draw=sk(l1=lambda.H,l2=lambda.A,action = "0"),
         lose=sk(l1=lambda.H,l2=lambda.A,action = "<"),
         pred=which.max(c(win,draw,lose))
         )

final$actual<-ifelse(pred_final$Goal.H>pred_final$Goal.A, 1, ifelse(pred_final$Goal.H==pred_final$Goal.A,2,3))


#confusion matrix
table(final$actual,final$pred)

```

## Bradley-Terry model (15p)

The library SportsAnalytics270 contains info on NBA regular season games.

### Model Building (10p)

You need to apply everything you learned on Bradley Terry model to NBA. Leave the last season out of the model.

```{r}
data(nba2009_2021)
```

#### Pre-processing
```{r}
# from slides
# creaating train test datasets

nba <- nba2009_2021 %>% select(SEASON_ID, home.TEAM_NAME, away.TEAM_NAME, home.WL) %>% 
          mutate(ht_w = ifelse(home.WL=="W",1,0),
                 at_w = ifelse(home.WL=="L",1,0),
                 home.TEAM_NAME = as.factor(home.TEAM_NAME),
                 away.TEAM_NAME = as.factor(away.TEAM_NAME))
# train test
train <- nba %>% filter(SEASON_ID!="2018")  %>% 
        group_by(home.TEAM_NAME, away.TEAM_NAME) %>% summarise(ht=sum(ht_w), at=sum(at_w))

test <- nba %>% filter(SEASON_ID=="2018")  %>% 
        group_by(home.TEAM_NAME, away.TEAM_NAME) %>% summarise(ht=sum(ht_w), at=sum(at_w))

```
#### Model

```{r}
BT_Model <- BTm(cbind(ht,at), home.TEAM_NAME, away.TEAM_NAME, data=train, id="team_")
# summary(BT_Model)/
```

### Abilities

```{r}
abilities <- as.data.frame(BTabilities(BT_Model))
abilities$team <- rownames(abilities)
abilities <- abilities[order(abilities$ability, decreasing = T),]

ggplot(data=abilities, aes(x=reorder(team,ability), y = ability))+geom_bar(stat="identity") +coord_flip()+
  labs(x="Teams", y="Ability to Win", title="Team vs Ability")
```


### Prediction (5p)

Make the prediction on the last season in the data and evaluate its perfromance.

```{r}
pred<-predict(BT_Model,newdata=test, type='response')

test$home_win<-pred
test$away_win<-1-pred
head(test)
```
